text: each step reads 3.44 gb of weights (2.82 gb of layers and 0.62 gb for the output head) plus the cache: 229 kb per context token per beam, about 1.2 gb for three beams at a 1,700-token context. at the measured 79 to 91 gb/s that caps a single clip near 26 steps per second with a short context and near 20 with a long one.
19.4 to 21.7 steps per second for one clip, about 85 to 95 percent of that ceiling. this is a plateau.

bound by gpu arithmetic. apple's matrix kernel measured 2.7 tflops here. a 2-minute prefill is about 5.9 tflop of work, so about 2.2 s at best, against 2.3 s now. a short prefill is about 0.24 s, of which 88 ms is widening the weights to 32-bit.

with three rows per thread sharing each weight read, a 12-row step costs about what a 3-row step did before: 51 ms against 103 ms. twelve medium clips run at 12.4x realtime cool and 9.8x warm, against 6x one at a time. wider than 12 rows gains nothing, and long clips gain less, because each new piece is still encoded and read in alone between steps.

same accuracy: met on the three golden clips, with at most 36 percent of the safety margin used. speed: 4.3x to 6.4x realtime for one clip. throughput: 12.4x for many short files cool, inside the plan's 12 to 20x estimate, and about 6x for mixed lengths. latency: 0.30 s to first text on a short file. live first text 0.46 to 0.76 s, then token by token.

read several pieces in together. each new piece is encoded and prefilled alone, and that is half the time of a batch of short clips. it needs proof that the matrix kernel gives a row the same bits at any row count.
log-softmax and top-k on the gpu, to drop the 1.8 mb logits readback per step. small.

the wait between live draft passes. each pass re-encodes the phrase, prefills it and re-decodes the unsettled tail before new text appears: 0.5 to 0.9 s at the 90th percentile. the 88 ms of weight widening per prefill is the cheapest part to remove, at the cost of 5.6 gb for a 32-bit copy.

energy, an instruments trace of where work ran, the noise run through a real input, and a proper cool-against-hot comparison. forty minutes of back-to-back runs took sustained throughput from about 6x to 4.3x on this fanless mac.

on a real iphone: the three golden clips give the reference text on an iphone 17 pro, but the token-level golden test has not run there, and the microphone, listen and record are untried. also unverified anywhere: voice processing, a full first-run download of the 4 gb checkpoint, and voiceover.

decode is bound by memory bandwidth. the three-row kernel reads about 86 gb/s alone in a microbenchmark, and inside a real step the layer matrices read about 77 gb/s (2.82 gb in 36.7 ms of a 52.6 ms step; the output head 7.6 ms, attention 6.8 ms). one clip decodes at 19.9 to 21.8 steps per second in the newest passing run. tried and dropped today: cpu time between steps (under 2 percent of a step), more weight loads in flight (no gain, the compiler already pipelines them), weights through threadgroup memory (slower, and not bit-identical), and widening the next matrix during the last multiply (inside noise; it would need a second queue). built: reading several pieces in one prefill, bit-identical, 27 to 39 percent less gpu time for groups of short pieces, but the scheduler gained nothing with it for twelve clips at once, so it is not used. the encoder no longer depends on the conv group. levers left, by size: in-step matrices at 77 gb/s against 86 gb/s alone, at most about a tenth of the layer time if closed; log-softmax and top-k on the gpu to drop the 1.8 mb logits readback per step, small; the wait between live draft passes, 0.5 to 0.9 s, of which the 88 ms weight widening per prefill is the cheapest part, at the cost of 5.6 gb for a 32-bit weight copy; and a scheduler that refills in groups, so the multi-piece prefill can pay. not measured: energy, a trace of where work ran, a controlled hot against cool comparison, and the golden test on a phone.
